title: Choosing generators of a regular prime with controlled annihilators (Ogoma)
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subset\Lambda$ an ideal and $\mathfrak q\subset\Lambda$ a prime ideal with $I\subset\mathfrak q$, and let $n,e\ge1$ be integers. Assume $\mathfrak q^n\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\subset I\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, where $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is the localization at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and that $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] of dimension $d$. Then there are $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_d\in\Lambda$ such that (1) the images of $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_d$ generate $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$; (2) $\pi_1^n,\dots,\pi_d^n\in I$; (3) for $i=1,\dots,d$, writing $M_i=\Lambda/(\pi_1^e,\dots,\pi_{i-1}^e)\Lambda$, one has $\{m\in M_i:\pi_im=0\}=\{m\in M_i:\pi_i^2m=0\}$, i.e. $\mathrm{Ann}_{M_i}(\pi_i)=\mathrm{Ann}_{M_i}(\pi_i^2)$. (Stacks writes 'there exists an $n>0$ and $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_d$', after having fixed $n$ in the hypotheses; its proof obtains (2) for the given $n$ from $\mathfrak q^n\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\subset I\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, so the $n$ in (2) is the given one, as stated here.)

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07FD (lemma-find-sequence, line 2314), Section 07FB; its proof uses Lemma Tag 07FC (lemma-ogoma, Ogoma), Algebra Lemmas Tag 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM) and Tag 07DV (lemma-regular-sequence-powers)

proof.text: Set $S=\Lambda\setminus\mathfrak q$, a multiplicative subset, so that $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}=S^{-1}\Lambda$ with the map $a\mapsto a/1$; $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, and every $s\in S$ maps to a unit $s/1$. Observation used below: if $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_d$ satisfy (1) and (2) and $s_1,\dots,s_d\in S$, then $s_1\pi_1,\dots,s_d\pi_d$ satisfy (1) and (2): $(s_i\pi_i)/1=(s_i/1)(\pi_i/1)$ with $s_i/1$ a unit, so the ideals generated in $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ agree, and $(s_i\pi_i)^n=s_i^n\pi_i^n\in I$ as $I$ is an ideal.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 07FD, lines 2338-2345 ('Note that (1) and (2) are preserved by further multiplying by elements of S')

proof.text: (Choice with (1).) Since $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is a regular local ring of dimension $d$, its maximal ideal $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is generated by $d$ elements $y_1,\dots,y_d$. Write $y_i=a_i/t_i$ with $a_i\in\Lambda$, $t_i\in S$, and put $\pi_i=a_i$. Then $\pi_i/1=(t_i/1)y_i$ with $t_i/1$ a unit, so $(\pi_1/1,\dots,\pi_d/1)=(y_1,\dots,y_d)=\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$: (1) holds. In particular $\pi_i/1\in\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ for every $i$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 07FD, line 2340 ('First pick pi_1,...,pi_d with (1) which is possible as Lambda_q is regular')

proof.text: (Achieving (2).) By step 2, $\pi_i^n/1=(\pi_i/1)^n\in\mathfrak q^n\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\subset I\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ by hypothesis, so $\pi_i^n/1=\sum_k(b_k/1)(c_k/t)$ with $b_k\in I$, $c_k\in\Lambda$, $t\in S$, i.e. $\pi_i^n/1=(\sum_kb_kc_k)/t$; by the definition of equality of fractions there is $u\in S$ with $u(t\pi_i^n-\sum_kb_kc_k)=0$, hence $s_i\pi_i^n\in I$ for $s_i=ut\in S$. Then $(s_i\pi_i)^n=s_i^{n-1}(s_i\pi_i^n)\in I$. Replacing each $\pi_i$ by $s_i\pi_i$ gives elements satisfying (2), and still (1) by step 1.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 07FD, lines 2341-2344 ('we can find s_1,...,s_d in S such that s_i pi_i^n in I. Replacing pi_i by s_i pi_i we get (2)')

proof.text: (Induction set-up.) For $t\in\{0,\dots,d\}$ consider the claim $P(t)$: there are $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_d\in\Lambda$ satisfying (1), (2), and (3) for $i=1,\dots,t$. By steps 2-3, $P(0)$ holds ((3) is then empty), and $P(d)$ is the lemma (for $d=0$ there is nothing more to do). Condition (3) for an index $i$ involves only $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_i$ (the module $M_i=\Lambda/(\pi_1^e,\dots,\pi_{i-1}^e)\Lambda$ and the element $\pi_i$), so replacing $\pi_{t+1}$ by $s\pi_{t+1}$ for some $s\in S$ keeps (3) for $i\le t$, and keeps (1), (2) by step 1. It remains to show: given $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_d$ with $P(t)$ and $t<d$, there is $s\in S$ such that (3) holds for $i=t+1$ after replacing $\pi_{t+1}$ by $s\pi_{t+1}$ (steps 5-7).

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 07FD, lines 2346-2347 and 2359-2360 ('Suppose that (3) holds for i=1,...,t ... By induction on t this produces a sequence satisfying (1), (2), and (3)')

proof.text: (Regular sequence in $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$.) By (1) the $d$ elements $\pi_1/1,\dots,\pi_d/1$ lie in and generate the maximal ideal $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ of the regular local ring $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ of dimension $d$, so by Algebra Lemma 00NQ they form a regular sequence in $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$. By Algebra Lemma 07DV applied to $M=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ with exponents $e_1=\dots=e_t=e$ and $e_{t+1}=\dots=e_d=1$, the sequence $\pi_1^e/1,\dots,\pi_t^e/1,\pi_{t+1}/1,\dots,\pi_d/1$ is a regular sequence in $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$; its condition (1) at index $t+1$ says that multiplication by $\pi_{t+1}/1$ is injective on $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/(\pi_1^e,\dots,\pi_t^e)\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$. Hence so is multiplication by $(\pi_{t+1}/1)^2$ (a composite of injective maps), and $\operatorname{Ker}(\pi_{t+1})=0=\operatorname{Ker}(\pi_{t+1}^2)$ on $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/(\pi_1^e,\dots,\pi_t^e)\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ (Stacks displays this with the index $i$ in place of $t+1$).

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 07FD, lines 2348-2357, citing Algebra Lemma Tag 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM) and Lemma Tag 07DV (lemma-regular-sequence-powers)

proof.text: (Passing to $S^{-1}M$.) Let $J=(\pi_1^e,\dots,\pi_t^e)\Lambda$ and $M=M_{t+1}=\Lambda/J$, a finitely generated $\Lambda$-module (generated by the class of $1$). Localizing the exact sequence $J\to\Lambda\to\Lambda/J\to0$ of $\Lambda$-modules at $S$ gives an exact sequence $S^{-1}J\to S^{-1}\Lambda\to S^{-1}M\to0$; the image of $S^{-1}J$ in $S^{-1}\Lambda=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is the set of $j/s$, $j\in J$, which is the ideal $(\pi_1^e/1,\dots,\pi_t^e/1)\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$. So $S^{-1}M\cong\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/(\pi_1^e,\dots,\pi_t^e)\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ as $\Lambda$-modules, and multiplication by $\pi_{t+1}$ on $S^{-1}M$ (which is $S^{-1}$ of multiplication by $\pi_{t+1}$ on $M$) corresponds to multiplication by $\pi_{t+1}/1$. By step 5, $\operatorname{Ker}(\pi_{t+1}:S^{-1}M\to S^{-1}M)=0=\operatorname{Ker}(\pi_{t+1}^2:S^{-1}M\to S^{-1}M)$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 07FD, lines 2355-2358 (the display over S^{-1}Lambda/(pi_1^e,...,pi_{i-1}^e), which Stacks identifies with S^{-1}M without comment)

proof.text: (Ogoma.) $\Lambda$ is Noetherian, $M$ is a finitely generated $\Lambda$-module, $S$ is multiplicative and by step 6 $\operatorname{Ker}(\pi_{t+1})=\operatorname{Ker}(\pi_{t+1}^2)$ on $S^{-1}M$; so Ogoma's lemma gives $s\in S$ with $\operatorname{Ker}(s^m\pi_{t+1}:M\to M)=\operatorname{Ker}((s^m\pi_{t+1})^2:M\to M)$ for every $m>0$; take $m=1$. Since for $a\in\Lambda$ the annihilator $\mathrm{Ann}_M(a)=\{x\in M:ax=0\}$ is $\operatorname{Ker}(a:M\to M)$, this says $\mathrm{Ann}_{M_{t+1}}(s\pi_{t+1})=\mathrm{Ann}_{M_{t+1}}((s\pi_{t+1})^2)$, where $M_{t+1}=\Lambda/(\pi_1^e,\dots,\pi_t^e)\Lambda$ does not change when $\pi_{t+1}$ is replaced. Replacing $\pi_{t+1}$ by $s\pi_{t+1}$ gives (3) for $i=t+1$, and by step 4 the new sequence satisfies $P(t+1)$. Induction on $t$ from $P(0)$ (step 4) gives $P(d)$, the lemma.

split_report.summary: Compared with Stacks 07FD word by word: Stacks fixes positive integers n, e in the hypotheses and then says 'there exists an n > 0 and pi_1,...,pi_d'; the proof (lines 2341-2344) obtains pi_i^n in I for the given n from q^n Lambda_q in I Lambda_q, so the existential n is a slip and the node's form (given n) is what the proof gives and what the citer lem-weil-pbc-popescu-resolve-separable uses (its n with q^n Lambda_q in h_A Lambda_q, e = 8c); the parenthesis of the statement was reworded to say so, otherwise the statement is unchanged. e only enters (3). Proof split in 7 steps following Stacks: lifting generators of q Lambda_q (regular local ring definition), clearing denominators to get (2), stability of (1),(2) under multiplication by S, induction on t, regular sequence pi_1^e..pi_t^e,pi_{t+1},... in Lambda_q via 00NQ (existing node lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence) and 07DV (existing node lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-powers, applied with exponents (e,..,e,1,..,1) so no initial-segment argument is needed), identification S^{-1}(Lambda/J) = Lambda_q/J Lambda_q (which Stacks leaves implicit; via lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact), and Ogoma 07FC (lem-weil-pbc-ogoma) with its exponent taken to be 1. Stacks' display uses index i where t+1 is meant. No new node was needed; all tags (07FD, 07FC, 00NQ, 07DV) verified in tags/tags.

reviewed.note: 7 steps follow Stacks 07FD: generators lifted from a regular system of parameters, (2) via q^n Lambda_q in I Lambda_q with the given n (Stacks' 'there exists an n' is a slip, as the proof shows), induction on t with 00NQ and 07DV nodes (existing, unsplit) for the regular sequence, S^{-1}M identified via the exactness leaf, Ogoma's node for (3). No new nodes. Tags 07FD, 07FC, 00NQ, 07DV verified.

lean.statement: theorem exists_generators_with_controlled_annihilators {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (I q : Ideal R) [q.IsPrime] (hIq : I ≤ q) (n e d : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (he : 0 < e) (hpow : (q ^ n).map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime q)) ≤ I.map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime q))) [IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime q)] (hdim : ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime q) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) : ∃ π : Fin d → R, Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i ↦ algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime q) (π i))) = q.map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime q)) ∧ (∀ i : Fin d, π i ^ n ∈ I) ∧ (∀ i : Fin d, {m : R ⧸ Ideal.span {x : R | ∃ j : Fin d, j < i ∧ x = π j ^ e} | π i • m = 0} = {m : R ⧸ Ideal.span {x : R | ∃ j : Fin d, j < i ∧ x = π j ^ e} | π i ^ 2 • m = 0})
